title: fix(service-print): a server print works under the console's default CSP (the ready wait passes a function, not a string)
body:

_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X5qLZ9SK4dTsHt1W8ph2VBe)_

Fixes #26664

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：服务端打印的 Chromium 驱动等待打印页就绪时，改为传一个函数谓词，不再传字符串。
- **为什么改**：默认部署下控制台 CSP 不含 `'unsafe-eval'`，字符串谓词每次轮询都要在页面里 eval，第二次轮询即抛 EvalError，所有服务端打印都失败。
- **风险与回滚**：只动 `chromium-driver.ts` 一处等待；就绪含义、超时、轮询间隔不变，控制台 CSP 不变。回滚即还原该文件。
- **先看**：`packages/services/service-print/src/chromium-driver.ts`（`printReady` 与 `waitForFunction` 那一行）；`chromium-driver.unit.test.ts` 末尾新增的两条。
- **两分钟验证**：`OS_TEST_PRINT_CHROMIUM_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-print exec vitest run src/chromium-driver.test.ts`，应见 CSP 那条在两种放置下都通过（main 上是 EvalError）。
- **需要你做的**：无，席位落地。

## What changes

`packages/services/service-print/src/chromium-driver.ts` waited for the print page with `page.waitForFunction(PRINT_READY_PREDICATE, …)`, where the predicate was a **string**. It is now a function, `printReady(stablePolls)`, passed as `page.waitForFunction(printReady, STABLE_POLLS, { timeout: remaining(), polling: POLL_INTERVAL_MS })`.

**Which evaluation path, and why `script-src` does not block it** (read in playwright-core 1.63.0, `lib/coreBundle.js` `waitForFunctionExpression`, and measured below). The wait installs a poller through the injected script's `evaluateHandle`, a DevTools `Runtime.callFunctionOn`. The poller's `predicate()` runs `globalThis.eval(expression)`:

- with a **string** (`isFunction: false`), on **every** poll. The first poll runs synchronously inside the DevTools call, where the inspector permits code generation; every later poll runs from a page `setTimeout`, where the page's CSP governs, and without `'unsafe-eval'` it throws EvalError. The predicate needs three stable polls, so the second poll always fails.
- with a **function** (`isFunction: true`), **once**: the first, synchronous poll caches the evaluated function (`evaledExpression`), and every later poll calls that cached function. No string is evaluated from a page timer, so the CSP has nothing to refuse.

The readiness meaning is unchanged: the same three conditions (a `[data-print-page]` root, `window.__objectui` present, `idle === true`), the same in-page run counter (`__objectstackPrintStable`), the same `STABLE_POLLS` (3), the same 100 ms polling and the same share of the one render budget. The page receives the function's text only, so the poll count it used to read from a template literal now arrives as its argument. The built output was read: tsup emits `printReady` as plain ES2020 in both `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.cjs`, with no injected helper names.

The console CSP (`packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts`) is not touched. `page.evaluate(FONTS_READY)` stays a string: it is evaluated synchronously inside its DevTools call, and the CSP leg below shows it passing.

A `patch` changeset on `@objectstack/service-print`.

## Tests

- `chromium-driver.unit.test.ts` (runs in CI, no browser): the staged page's `waitForFunction` must receive a **function**, `STABLE_POLLS` as its argument, `polling: 100` and a timeout inside the budget. A second case runs the received function against a staged `document` / `__objectui` and pins the meaning: false with no console, false when idle with no root, false with the root while busy, then exactly `STABLE_POLLS` idle polls to true, and a busy poll resets the run.
- `chromium-driver.test.ts` (real Chromium, both placements): the fixture now also serves the print page under the console's default policy (`script-src 'self' 'nonce-…' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, the script carrying the nonce), and a new case per placement renders it.
- The render dogfood (`packages/qa/dogfood/test/print-service-render.dogfood.test.ts`, which carries the named-page leg from #26662) is unchanged; it is the end-to-end reading below.

## Acceptance notes

- CI skips both real-Chromium files (`describe.skipIf(!CHROMIUM)` / `!CHROMIUM || !CONSOLE_BUILT`): Test Core has no Chromium and no console bundle. The unit test is the guard CI runs. Turning the render tests on in CI is a CI-provisioning question and is not done here.
- `page.evaluate(FONTS_READY)` and the predicate's first poll rely on DevTools-initiated evaluation being exempt from the page's `'unsafe-eval'` check, which is Chromium's behaviour today and is what playwright-core's own function-predicate path relies on.

## Verification

All readings at head `dfd3fc087`, with `OS_PAGE_REACT_ENABLED` (and legacy `OS_PAGE_REACT`) unset, Chromium `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium`, console bundle from `pnpm console:build`.

<details><summary>Red on main's driver (base 1685a06dd): EvalError</summary>

`chromium-driver.ts` byte-equal to `origin/main`, the new tests committed:

- `vitest run src/chromium-driver.unit.test.ts src/chromium-driver.test.ts`: Tests 4 failed, 16 passed (20). Both unit cases fail; the CSP case fails on both placements with `The print engine failed at the local executable /opt/pw-browsers/chromium: page.waitForFunction: EvalError: Evaluating a string as JavaScript violates the following Content Security Policy directive because 'unsafe-eval' is not an allowed source of script: script-src 'self' 'nonce-print-fixture-nonce' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` (and the same at the remote endpoint).
- Dogfood `print-service-render.dogfood.test.ts` + `print-service-named-page.dogfood.test.ts`: Tests 6 failed, 6 passed (12). All 6 render legs (invoice, named print page, revoke-after-failure; local and remote) fail with the EvalError under the console's real nonce policy. The named-page file uses a stand-in driver and passes either way.

</details>
